methodologyNotes: Covers standalone battery-powered portable audio field recorders that write to removable media and are sold at a published US price. Includes handheld stereo recorders and compact multitrack location recorder/mixers. Excludes smartphone/USB microphones, rack and studio interfaces with no internal recording, lavalier/wireless mic systems, and dictation voice memo pens. Price is US MSRP (or typical street price where MSRP is not published), in USD. xlrInputs is the count of dedicated XLR or XLR/TRS combo mic/line input jacks (0 if none). maxTracks is the maximum number of tracks recorded simultaneously to a single project (includes any auto-generated stereo mix track). maxBitDepthBits is the highest recording bit depth in bits (24 or 32). maxSampleRateKhz is the highest linear-PCM sample rate in kHz. thirtyTwoBitFloat is a boolean: true if the recorder captures native 32-bit float WAV. phantomPower is a boolean: true if it supplies 48V phantom power on at least one input. builtInMics is a boolean: true if fixed onboard microphones are included. storageType is an enum of the removable card slot(s): microSD, SD, dual-SD, or dual-microSD. displayType is an enum: mono-LCD, color-LCD, or color-touch. powerSource is an enum of the primary supply: AA, AAA, Li-ion, or USB-C. batteryLifeHrs is the manufacturer-rated continuous recording time in hours on the primary power source; null if not disclosed. weightGrams is body weight without batteries in grams.

products.name: Zoom F3
products.priceNote: Typical/launch US street price $329.99. The dated Creative Field Recording first-look review (2022-03-30) states it multiple times verbatim ("At $329.99, the Zoom F3 is the cheapest 32-bit recorder on the market"), and Walmart currently lists it as "Now $329.99" (was $349.99, sold by Adorama). Zoom's own product page showed no price (item marked unavailable).
products.provenance: The official Zoom F3 product page (source) confirms this exact model: a 2-channel/2-track field recorder with two locking XLR MIC/LINE inputs, 44.1/48/88.2/96/192 kHz 32-bit float WAV recording, +24/48 V phantom power, a 96x64 backlit mono LCD, microSDHC/SDXC storage (to 1 TB), USB-C, and about 8 hours on two AA alkaline batteries; it displayed no price (item shown as unavailable). The dated Creative Field Recording first-look review (2022-03-30, corroboration) confirms the same F3 model and specs (192 kHz/32-bit, XLR-only inputs, 2 AA / 8 hours, 242 g including batteries) and states the price as $329.99, matching Walmart's current $329.99 (was $349.99). Weight is only ever quoted including batteries (242 g), so the without-batteries figure required by the methodology is left null rather than guessed.

Precision Camera similarly confirms the same model and specs. No fetched page states a release date, so releaseDate is left null.

products.name: Zoom H6essential

products.provenance: The official Tascam US spec page (tascam.com/us/product/dr-40x) confirms this exact model, the DR-40X 4-channel portable field recorder, via its full spec table: 4-channel recording, WAV/BWF at 16/24-bit and 44.1/48/96 kHz, dual Neutrik XLR/TRS combo inputs with +48V phantom power, stereo built-in unidirectional condenser mics, SD/SDHC/SDXC media, a 128x64 graphic LCD, 3 AA power, approx. 18-hour alkaline recording time, and 213 g weight; no 32-bit float is offered (max 24-bit), so thirtyTwoBitFloat is false. products.name: Sony PCM-D10
products.priceNote: Sony's official pro.sony US product page lists "$499.99 U.S. List Price" (US MSRP). Corroborated by the transom.org June 2019 review, which states the price as "$500 USD," and by electronics.sony.com ("$499.99").
products.provenance: Sony's official pro.sony US product page confirms the exact model "PCM-D10" at "$499.99 U.S. List Price," recording Hi-Res audio "at up to 192 kHz/24 bit," with a "twin XLR/TRS jack" for "two-channel recording" carrying "independent 48-V phantom power," "three-way built-in mics," "up to 256 GB of SD card storage," and power via "dry cell batteries (4xAA)" or USB Type-C. The dated transom.org June 2019 review independently confirms the model identity, the "$500 USD" price, and the "24-bit and 192 kHz" maximum, and notes it "cannot record the built-in mics and the external XLR inputs simultaneously" (max two channels). No 32-bit float capability is stated (max is 24-bit), and the only disclosed weight (480 g) explicitly includes batteries whereas the schema requires body weight without batteries, so weightGrams, displayType, and batteryLifeHrs are left null rather than guessed.
